name: Jehallelel
title: Levite and patriarch in Judah
summary: Jehallelel is a biblical figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles. There are two individuals with this name: one belonging to the tribe of Judah and another who was a Levite during King Hezekiah's time. The name means 'he shall praise God' and reflects a worshipful praise of the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Jehallelel's lineage in Judah
keyEvents.description: Jehallelel is mentioned as a descendant in the tribe of Judah with four sons: Sif, Sisna, Tilon and Anaeli.

keyEvents.title: The Levites' cleansing of the temple
keyEvents.description: Another Jehallelel, father of the Levite Azariah, participated in the cleansing of the temple during King Hezekiah's reforms.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's temple reform
keyEvents.description: King Hezekiah commanded the Levites to consecrate themselves and cleanse the house of the Lord. Asaiah, son of Jehallelel, was among the Levites who obeyed the king's command.

keyEvents.title: The Obedience of the Levites
keyEvents.description: The Levites, including Asaiah, son of Jehallelel from the clan of Merari, gathered to carry out the cleansing work in the temple as ordered by the king.

keyEvents.title: Restoration of Worship
keyEvents.description: After the temple was cleansed by the Levites, including descendants of Jehallelel, worship was restored in Jerusalem under Hezekiah's leadership.
